findings.F1: The book loses because it is short most of the time in coins that rise. It is short on 69 % to 80 % of bars, with a mean position of -0.41 to -0.58. Its gain from the market's own rise is negative on every coin (-0.031 % to -0.069 % per bar). Its timing gain is positive on 5 of 6 coins (+0.018 % to +0.060 % per bar) but smaller. So the idea's total move per case is -0.47 % over 5 days, against a cost of 0.19 %.
findings.F2: The book stays short even where no cluster of past lows sits near the close. On bars with no swing low within 3 % above the close, its mean position is -0.36 and it is short 68 % of the time (13,384 bars), losing 0.039 % per bar. The standardised, negated forecast turns any low above the close, however far, into a short.
findings.F3: The short gains only where the level is close. With the nearest past low within 1 % above the close, the book gains +0.13 % per bar (1,932 bars). With it 7 % to 15 % above, it loses 0.10 % per bar (1,612 bars). With it more than 15 % above, it loses 0.13 % per bar (1,008 bars).
findings.F4: The count of swing lows within 3 % above the close grades the next 5 days' move (unusual move, non-overlapping cases):
findings.F5: The graded fall is broad. With 3 or more such lows, the 5-day unusual move is negative on all 6 coins (-0.8 % to -6.1 %) and in 7 of 8 years (-1.7 % to -7.2 %; 2020 is the exception at +4.5 %).
findings.F6: The fall is concentrated when the close is below its 50-day average.
findings.F7: The book's own forecast is graded but too wide. Short cases in the top half of |forecast| have an unusual short-side move of +0.86 % (t 3.09, n 1,179). The weakest quarter has -0.44 % (n 590). The weak cases dilute the edge toward the verdict's +0.12 %, and each one pays the coin's rise.

ideas.idea: When a coin's daily close sits just below prices where it turned up several times in the past 90 days, it tends to fall over the next 5 days, and the more such past turning-up lows lie within a few percent above the close, the larger the fall, only while the close is below its 50-day average price.
ideas.consequence: A close under a tight cluster of past lows in a coin already below its 50-day average is a reason to be short for 5 days, and a single or distant past low above the close is no reason to be short at all.
ideas.name: clustered broken support in downtrend

ideas.idea: When a coin's daily close sits just below prices where it turned up several times in the past 90 days, it tends to fall over the next 5 days, and the more such past turning-up lows lie within a few percent above the close and the nearer the closest of them, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A short on a broken support is worth taking only when several past lows are bunched just above the close, because a lone or far-off past low carries no fall and leaves the short paying the coin's rise.
ideas.name: tight cluster of broken lows
